1.explanation:
• DataTable/DataTable.mdx: the primary documentation for the DataTable component, showing how it and its sub-components are structured internally and intended to be consumed.
• DataTable/docs/overview.mdx: the overview guide with usage examples, including direct imports of TableContainer, Table, etc., which clarifies the correct import patterns.
• DataTable/stories/dynamic-content/ and DataTable/stories/expansion/: live code examples (Storybook stories) demonstrating how DataTable and its sub-components are imported and used, which help reproduce and compare the broken vs. working patterns.
• DataTable/state/: contains the hooks and state utilities (e.g. useDataTable) that power the DataTable implementation; understanding these helps explain why destructuring from DataTable itself fails to yield valid React components.
• DataTable/tools/: includes build or export helper scripts that define the module’s public API surface—key to understanding why sub-components aren’t available as properties on the default DataTable export.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots show a minimal React app using Carbon’s DataTable. In the first image we see a single default import of DataTable from '@carbon/react', followed immediately by a destructuring assignment pulling out TableContainer, Table, TableHead, TableRow, TableHeader, TableBody, and TableCell from DataTable. This causes runtime React errors: “React.createElement: type is invalid… got undefined,” because those sub-components aren’t exposed that way in v11. The second screenshot shows the fix: commenting out the destructure and instead importing each component directly (import { DataTable, TableContainer, Table, TableHead, … } from '@carbon/react'), which restores the table UI without errors.
